 If you have an iPhone , AirPods , and an Apple Watch , congrats! You have the holy trinity of Apple products. But keeping all these gadgets powered up can be annoying, since they all have individual cables and proprietary charging solutions. Why deal with all that hassle when the best 3-in-1 Apple charging stations can accommodate everything? Our Best Wireless Chargers guide has a few recommendations, but many more great docking systems exist for Apple devices. After years of testing 3-in-1 Apple charging stations, these are my favorites. If you want one you can take on a trip, check out my new Best Apple 3-in-1 Travel Chargers guide.
 Be sure to read our other Apple guides , including the Best MagSafe Wireless Chargers , Best MagSafe Power Banks , Best MagSafe Accessories , Best iPhone 17 Cases , and Best iPad Accessories .
 Updated September 2026: I added chargers from Nimble, Mophie, Journey, and OtterBox, removed some older devices, and updated prices.

 Belkin
 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand
 $109 $98 (10% off) Shop
 $90 Amazon
 $80 Best Buy
 This classy chrome charging tree suspends two of your Apple gadgets in midair, with a spot for the AirPods case on the broad circular base. It recharges your iPhone at up to 15-watt charging speed and can also fast-charge the Apple Watch Series 7 or newer (and older Apple Watch models at a slower rate). Drop the AirPods Pro (or AirPods with wireless charging case) onto the base, and you'll be topping up all these devices from a single outlet. Aside from the Qi2 certification , the base is now more rounded than the original version, and the iPhone charging pad tilts to your preferred angle. Everything sits securely in place, and you can even flip your iPhone into landscape orientation to watch a video while it charges or to trigger StandBy mode , a feature Apple added in iOS 17 that turns the iPhone into a clock on your nightstand with weather information when you put it in landscape orientation on a wireless charger. (The screen dims if you have an iPhone with an always-on display; if not, you can tap the screen to see the time.) The braided USB-C cable is permanently attached.

 Nomad
 Stand One Max
 $169 Nomad
 For speedy charging (Qi2 25W for your iPhone and fast charging for your Apple Watch) in a seriously classy, glossy black design reminiscent of a Steinway grand piano, Nomad’s new Stand One Max is an excellent 3-in-1 charger. The pad is angled to accommodate landscape or portrait orientation for your iPhone (or other Qi2 phone), and the Apple Watch puck sits up for Nightstand mode, with a subtle hollow behind it for your wireless earbuds case. You also get a lovely, braided, 6.6-foot USB-C cable in the box. The base is heavy enough that you can pick your phone off one-handed without it toppling. Considering the relatively high price, it’s a shame there’s no power adapter included. You need one rated at 40 watts. I like Nomad’s 40W Slim Adapter ($25) .

 ESR
 Qi2 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station
 $80 $30 (63% off) Amazon
 By far the cheapest Qi2-certified 3-in-1 charger I've come across, I was surprised by how much I liked this ESR charger. The magnetic iPhone pad is secure and charges at 15 watts, the design is compact, and it comes with a charging brick and cable. The Apple Watch charger is a separate unit that slots into the back. That means you can take it with you (it simply needs a USB-A port to plug into), though I instantly lost the cap. This charger also works for StandBy mode or watching video in landscape orientation. There is a new version of this stand with Qi2 25W support, but it's far more expensive for very little gain.

 Nimble
 Podium 3-in-1 Wireless Charger
 $130 Amazon
 $140 Nimble
 $140 Apple
 Maybe you don’t want to see your phone or watch screen when you’re trying to sleep. The latest version of Nimble’s 3-in-1 Podium charger enables your gadgets to lie flat, happily out of sight until morning. The phone and Apple Watch pads can also pop up to use StandBy or Nightstand mode on your devices, though, if you want. The flat phone charging pad can also charge any older Qi devices you have. It supports Qi2 25W to fast charge your iPhone, with pads for AirPods and an Apple Watch. The Apple Watch charging is slow though, so it's best left overnight. The base is weighty, and it comes in black or white. A USB-C cable and 36W power adapter come in the box. Nimble also uses recycled materials wherever possible, has multiple certifications and offers a free e-waste recycling program.
 Specs 
 Charging (per coil): 25 watts, 3.5 watts, 5 watts 
 Extra ports: None 
 In the box: 5-foot USB-C to USB-C cable and 36-watt power adapter 
 Warranty: 2 years

 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Photograph: Simon Hill

 Belkin
 UltraCharge Pro Wireless Charging Station
 $130 Amazon
 $130 Belkin
 We already have a Belkin as our top pick, but the newer UltraCharge Pro has some seriously compelling features. This isn’t just a Qi2 charger, it is Qi2.2, branded as Qi2 25W, which can charge compatible iPhones and Qi2 phones at up to 25 watts (I tested with the Pixel 10 Pro XL). You also get a fast-charging Apple Watch shelf tucked around back and a standard 5-watt AirPods pad below. The soft-touch finish comes in sand or black, and the chrome frame provides some contrast. The main pad is hinged, so you can find your preferred angle for StandBy mode, and it has a built-in fan to keep things cool at the higher charging rate. Mercifully, there’s a switch to turn the fan off when you want to sleep, as it does make a perceptible whine. The detachable USB-C cable is a generous 5 feet, and there’s a 45-watt power supply in the box.
 Specs 
 Charging (per coil): 25 watts, 5 watts, 5 watts 
 Extra ports: None 
 In the box: 45-watt power supply, USB-C cable (5 feet/1.5 meters) 
 Warranty: 2 years

 Mophie
 MagSafe 3-in-1 Extendable Wireless Charging Stand
 $150 $76 (49% off) Amazon
 $150 $60 (60% off) Best Buy
 Maybe you charge your iPhone at a standing desk. Or perhaps you want a more versatile charger. Enter Mophie's extendable wireless charging stand. The 15-watt iPhone charger sits atop a telescoping pole that can extend from 7.5 to 16 inches, and that means it doubles as a tripod of sorts—handy if you want to film a quick video or more comfortably take video calls. There's some flex in the charging pad too, so you can tilt it slightly up or down. You have to twist the pole slightly and then pull on it to extend, and while it's not the smoothest experience, it does the job and stays put. Attached to the bottom section of the pole is the Apple Watch charger, which supports fast charging. You can pop a pair of wireless earbuds, AirPods or otherwise, on the charging cradle on the metal base. Mophie includes a proprietary charger, but it's removable. — Julian Chokkattu

 Zens
 Nightstand Charger Pro 2
 $100 Amazon
 $100 Zens
 With a weighty base, an adjustable Qi2/MagSafe charging pad, and a fold-out Apple Watch charger around the back, this Zens 2-in-1 is ideal for folks with an iPhone and Apple Watch. The Apple Watch pad folds out of the back, tucking your watch out of sight and allowing room for the strap to droop. The pad works great with StandBy mode. You can also fold the pad flat and charge AirPods or other phones if you need to, just not at the same time as your iPhone. Sadly, this has a barrel port for the provided cable and charger (USB-C would be better), the Apple Watch charger can be a little stiff and tricky to fold out, and it’s pricey, but I love the quality, look, and feel.
 Photograph: Julian Chokkattu
 Save to wishlist 
 Belkin
 UltraCharge 2-in-1 Foldable Magnetic Wireless Charger (Qi2 25W)
 $60 Shop
 $60 $50 (17% off) Amazon
 $60 Belkin
 Belkin's UltraCharge 2-in-1 unseats our previous favorite, the BoostCharge Pro 2-in-1 , which is still a great option. However, the latest model features Qi2 25W charging support to charge compatible devices even faster. It also has a folding design, allowing you to take it with you on the go, but it also works great as a permanent charger for your desk or nightstand. Over on the back, there's a spot to place AirPods or any wireless earbuds with wireless charging. What's also great is the spare USB-C port—you can pop in a cable to charge your Apple Watch at 5 watts (or another device); it just won't charge very fast. (Belkin also has a 3-in-1 version of this model if you want a dedicated spot for the Apple Watch.) Best of all, Belkin includes a very compact 45-watt power adapter and a USB-C to USB-C cable, which is better than many other wireless chargers that cost more. It's a nifty little thing, and looks great in blue. — Julian Chokkattu 
 iOttie Velox Duo for $60 : This was our 2-in-1 pick for a while. The black-and-gold combo looks great, the magnet is strong, and there’s a weighted base. On the downside, it only charges iPhones at up to 7.5 watts. The permanently attached USB-C cable is a good length, but you do have to provide a wall adapter.
 Belkin BoostCharge Pro 2-in-1 Wireless Charging Dock with MagSafe for $120 : This was our old 2-in-1 pick for iPhone and Apple Watch. I like the soft-touch finish, the pad on top can move through 70 degrees, and the shelf for your Apple Watch works with any strap. The braided USB-C cable is permanently attached, but you get a 30-watt wall charger in the box. I don’t remember having issues when I first tested, but using it again, I found the weight of the camera end of my iPhone 14 Pro caused it to slowly droop when in StandBy mode. It’s also kinda pricey.
 Belkin BoostCharge Pro 2-in-1 MagSafe-Compatible Wireless Charging Pad for $80 : Qi2 support provides magnetic alignment for your iPhone and delivers 15 watts of charging, and there’s a spot for AirPods on this compact dual pad. A USB-C port allows you to charge something else, such as an Apple Watch, and you get a 5-foot USB-C cable and 30W power supply in the box. There is also a 3-in-1 pad ($110) that adds an Apple Watch charger on the right side.
 More 3-in-1 Chargers to Consider
 We have tested several other 3-in-1 Apple charging stations. Here are a few we liked:
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Save to wishlist 
 Journey
 Nova 3-in-1 Fast Wireless Charging Station
 $140 Journey
 With a refreshingly different look, the Nova from Journey is one of the most stylish 3-in-1 chargers I’ve tested. I love the black and walnut finish. Your Qi2 phone can charge at up to 15 watts; there’s a fast-charging Apple Watch pad that pops up around the back, and the space in the middle can charge AirPods at 5 watts. There’s also a handy night light with a touch-sensitive button that’s just enough to see what you’re doing. It’s compact and comes with a USB-C cable, but no power adapter, and I found the magnetic front a little weak.
 OtterBox 3-in-1 Charging Stand for $140 : This solid, fairly compact aluminum 3-in-1 charging station can charge all your Apple gadgets (25W for iPhone, 5W for Apple Watch, 5W for AirPods) and comes with a 6.6-foot cable and a 45-watt wall charger. While this new version of OtterBox’s 3-in-1 stand supports Qi2 25W, the design is unchanged, so you still can’t alter the angle of the pads. The integrated Apple Watch charger allows for Nightstand mode, but it is the weak link here, and I sometimes find my watch twists slightly.
 Noco X Grid XDS3.
 Photograph: Simon Hill 
 Noco X Grid XDS3 for $130 : Well made, with an eye-catching design, this 3-in-1 charger has a wide base that’s great for stability. It’s easy to remove your iPhone one-handed too, though it does have a relatively large footprint. It’s a bit bulky to travel with. You can stick your Qi2 phone to the pad in portrait or landscape, and the large bottom 5W pad is suitable for AirPods or even a second phone. You also get an adapter, generous 6.5-foot braided USB-C cable, and plug adapters for different countries in the box. It supports Apple Watch fast charging, but I didn’t like the way my Apple Watch tended to tilt to one side, and the charging pad positions are fixed (you can’t change the angle).
 Twelve South HiRise 3 Deluxe for $100 : Twelve South's 3-in-1 is an elegant wireless charger for the nightstand and gives the iPhone plenty of breathing room to rotate it to landscape mode and take advantage of StandBy. I like that the iPhone charger can swivel up and down. On the base is a fast charger for the Apple Watch that you can flip up, and the back has a spot for the AirPods or another wireless earbuds case. It's nice and weighty and doesn't slide around easily. It comes with a proprietary, removable charging cable, along with a charging brick, and international plug adapters for the US, UK, EU, and AU.
 Anker Prime 3-in-1.
 Photograph: Simon Hill 
 Anker Prime 3-in-1 Charging Station for $230 : Sporting a tree design similar to our top pick from Belkin, the very latest Qi2 25W charging, fast Apple Watch charging, active cooling, and an interactive display, this is perhaps the most feature-packed 3-in-1 charger on the market. You can connect via Bluetooth and configure in the app to set wallpapers for the clock, schedule night mode to dim the display and turn off the cooling, and track your charging stats in a table. I’m just not sure it’s worth the premium. The finicky touch display is flat, so you have to sit up to see it, and it looks a bit cheap to me. It also feels superfluous when your iPhone already offers Standby mode.
 Anker MagGo Wireless Charging Station Stand for $111 : This good-looking 3-in-1 charging tree is more affordable than our top pick, boasts Qi2 certification for 15-watt charging, and comes with a charger and cable. It just misses out on a place above because of the offset pad for the Apple Watch. It is slippery, so your Apple Watch may tilt, though I never had an issue with it not charging. Anker included stickers to combat this, but they are a fiddly and inelegant solution. It’s also a shame that the main pad for your iPhone is fixed, so you can’t adjust the angle. But these are minor gripes.
 Anker 3-in-1 Cube with MagSafe for $130 : This dinky, dense, 2.5-inch cube from Anker was our previous compact pick. It has a MagSafe pad on top (15 watts), and the top section hinges to a 60-degree angle, revealing a charging surface for your AirPods. The small pop-out shelf on the side has a built-in Apple Watch fast charger. You get a 5-foot cable and a 30-watt charger in the box.
 Zens Office Charger Pro 3
 Photograph: Simon Hill 
 Zens Office Charger Pro 3 for $85 : I’m a fan of some of the interesting, out-of-the-box designs that Zens turns out, but this 3-in-1, while well-made and perfectly functional, doesn’t really stand out. It’s Qi2 certified (15W for iPhone, 5W for Apple Watch, 5W for AirPods), looks nice, and comes with the cable and charger, though it has a barrel port.
 Lululook 3-in-1 Charging Station for $60 : This is a perfectly competent 3-in-1 with Qi2 certification (15W for iPhone, 5W for Apple Watch, 5W for AirPods). It’s compact, you can angle the iPhone pad, and I like the gold finish of my review unit, but I prefer the Twelve South above, or the ESR if you don’t want to spend as much.
 QDOS SnapStand 3-in-1 for £80 : This clever design feels sturdy and comes flat, and you can fold out and angle a magnetic pad for charging your iPhone (StandBy mode works fine). There’s a pop-out Apple Watch charger around the back, and the base has a pad for your AirPods. You get a black USB-C cable, but you’ll need a charger (at least 25W). I like that it’s partly made from recycled materials, and it folds away very neatly, but the charging speeds are relatively slow (7.5 watts for the iPhone and 2.5 watts for the Apple Watch).
 Satechi 3-in-1 Magnetic Wireless Charging Stand for $130 : This compact, attractive 3-in-1 is a little smaller than the Belkin, so it doesn't take up too much room, and it folds down compactly for travel. The aluminum build is attractive and sturdy (the iPhone mount is made of stainless steel). This is on former reviews editor Adrienne So's bedside table, and it recharges her Apple Watch Ultra 2 from 70 percent to full in around 30 minutes.
 Case-Mate Fuel 3-in-1 Foldable for $58 : Finished in a classy gray material, this 3-in-1 charges an iPhone in a case or any Qi smartphone, and it's easy to fold flat and pack in a bag. It also has a built-in Apple Watch charger and a spot for AirPods. A cable and a 45-watt charger are included. I also tested the solid Case-Mate Fuel 4-in-1 ($150) , which is quite good, but the unnecessary LEDs and Fuel logo put me off.
 Best 4-in-1 Chargers
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Photograph: Simon Hill
 Save to wishlist 
 Mophie
 4-in-1 Wireless Charge Stand
 $180 Mophie
 $180 Apple
 The whole point of a 3-in-1 is to reduce clutter and cables while still getting all your devices charged. And if you have an extra device, a 4-in-1 is one step better. This stand has a lovely compact design with a tilting Qi2 25W pad for your phone, an Apple Watch charger around the back, and an indented pad on the base for your AirPods. That's all familiar. What elevates it is the retractable USB-C cable that unfurls from the back and can deliver up to 60 watts. My wife uses it for her Oura charger, but she can also plug in her MacBook when it’s running low. It’s pricey, but there’s a 5-foot USB-C cable and a 100W wall adapter in the box. The gold finish is nice, too, but you can also opt for black or white.
 Zens 4-in-1 Modular Wireless Charger with iPad Charging Stand for $130 : If you also own an iPad, why not a 4-in-1 charging station? Zens’ modular design has a main stand for your iPad, a MagSafe pad in front to float your iPhone, and a slight indentation to charge AirPods below. The Apple Watch charger is a separate section that attaches magnetically (on either side) and holds your Watch in horizontal Nightstand mode. It feels durable with a grippy, rubbery, flecked black finish made from recycled plastic. You get a 65-watt power adapter, power cable, and adapter plugs for the US, UK, and EU, which is quite handy. The main drawback with this is the large size, and you have to connect a cable to the USB-C port on the side to charge your iPad.
 Scosche Baselynx 2.0 Modular Charging Station for $100 : What if three spots are not enough? Scosche has you covered with this modular charging station. The basic stand is a 2-in-1 for your iPhone and AirPods, but you can add an Apple Watch charger, a toast rack-style vertical station with USB-C ports, or even an AC outlet with USB-C port, for a big combined charger ($230) . The trouble is, it gets quite big and expensive as you add modules, and I don’t love the way it looks, but it’s a neat idea.
 Avoid These Chargers
 Photograph: Simon Hill 
 Not every charger will be a winner. Here are the ones we didn't like.
 Infinacore T3 Pro : The T3 Pro is a 3-in-1 stand that looks and feels very cheap, and it got warm when charging my iPhone. Its saving grace is that it is cheap. It also has Qi2 certification and works with StandBy mode. I also tried the fold-out triple pad Infinacore T3 Wireless Charging Station . Aside from the ugly plastic design, the weak magnets meant it did not work well when folded into the triangular configuration (this also blocks a pad).
 Groov-e Asteria Wireless Charging Station with Alarm Clock : There’s a small clock on the front of this charging station, which can accommodate an iPhone, AirPods on a pad around back, and an Apple Watch up top. It feels and looks very cheap, slides around a little too easily, the magnet is weak, and the clock seems redundant when you can set your iPhone in StandBy mode. I also tried the Triton 3-in-1 folding pad , and it was okay . They are very affordable, but you must provide your own power adapter.
 Zike 3-in-1 Z557C Stand : This 3-in-1 charger works perfectly well, but there are several better options above. The iPhone pad allows for StandBy mode but is not adjustable. The Apple Watch pad flips up or can be laid flat, and there’s a spot for AirPods on the gray felt pad. It has a barrel port, so you must use the supplied power adapter. What I really dislike about this charger is the ridiculously bright, utterly pointless white LED on the front that stays on the entire time.
 Alogic Matrix Ultimate : This 3-in-1 charger has a folding design, supports fast charging, includes a detachable 5,000-mAh power bank, and comes with a nice pouch, but it is kinda bulky, and the white finish picks up dust and smudges very easily. I have also had issues with other Alogic batteries failing and not supplying the stated capacity.
 STM Goods ChargeTree Go : This charging tree station folds flat and can charge a trio of Apple gadgets. But there’s no quick-charge support, my Apple Watch kept sliding out of place during the night, and there’s no adapter included. It’s not cheap either.
 A Quick Primer on MagSafe 
 AccordionItemContainerButton 
 Most of the wireless chargers in this guide are MagSafe wireless chargers or Qi2 certified . That means they take advantage of the magnets embedded in the back of the iPhone 12 , iPhone 13 , iPhone 14 , iPhone 15 , iPhone 16 , and iPhone 17 range. I cannot stress this enough: If you buy a case, ensure it is a MagSafe case . We have several third-party options in the linked case guides above. A normal iPhone case will weaken the pull of the magnets in the device and will not stick to MagSafe accessories well.
 What's the point of MagSafe? You don't have to worry about misalignment with the wireless charger, meaning you won't wake up to a dead iPhone. Technically, this perfect alignment enables chargers to deliver faster 15-watt charging. MagSafe is also available in the AirPods charging case (depending on your model ). Apple's AirPods and AirPods Pro with the wireless charging case will work with nearly all of the standard Qi wireless charging pads on these chargers (as will many third-party wireless earbuds ), but if you have AirPods with MagSafe, then you can hook them up to the magnetic mounts as well. If you don't have a MagSafe iPhone, then your device won't be able to attach to these chargers, though we do have some recommendations for older iPhones (and the iPhone 16e ).
 What About Qi2? 
 AccordionItemContainerButton 
 Qi2 is the latest wireless charging standard , and Apple worked with the Wireless Power Consortium to develop it. Compared to the original Qi standard, it brings MagSafe-style magnetic charging, faster charging rates, and improved efficiency—but where MagSafe is an Apple technology designed for Apple products, any device can support Qi2. Apple updated the iPhone 12 and newer to support Qi2, so Qi2 should be a term you look for when shopping for a magnetic wireless charger. Qi2 Android phones are still thin on the ground right now—it's officially available in Google's Pixel 10 series —though Qi2 Ready phones add magnets using a compatible case . Expect more Qi2 Android phones soon. A Qi2 charger can charge your iPhone and any other Qi2 phones.
 While Qi2 charging generally goes up to 15 watts, the Qi2.2 update, branded as Qi2 25W, can go up to 25 watts. But support for Qi2 25W is currently very limited, and includes the iPhone 17 range and the Pixel 10 Pro XL.
 What Are StandBy Mode and Nightstand Mode? 
 AccordionItemContainerButton 
 You'll see us bring up two specific modes throughout this guide: StandBy mode and Nightstand mode . What are they?
 StandBy mode was introduced in iOS 17 . When you place your iPhone on a charger in landscape orientation, it will turn the screen into a dock of sorts, showing the clock (with different designs you can choose from), photos from your library, or widgets. If you have an iPhone that supports an always-on screen, you can choose to have the display automatically turn off after some time when the iPhone isn't in use or if the room is dark. Head to Settings > Standby to customize it.
 Nightstand mode has long been around on the Apple Watch. Basically, when the watch is sitting upright and charging, the clockface will stay on so you can always tell the time. You can customize this on your Apple Watch by heading to Settings > General > Nightstand mode .

 It can feel a little crowded when fully loaded, but I appreciate the space-saving design when packing a bag. While you can find faster options below with chargers that feature Qi2 25W, it's not widely supported and makes little difference if you charge your devices overnight.

 Other Good 3-in-1 Travel Chargers

 Kuxiu Qi2 25W Travel Charging Station for $78 : This charger folds down to an impressively small package, and it feels sturdy with a silicone-covered metal construction. It can hit 25 watts for supported Qi2 W25 phones, comes in a few different finishes, and ships with a 45-watt power adapter and USB-C cable in the box. Unfortunately, I don’t like the way it looks, and I found it awkward to get all three devices charging at once. It’s actually so compact that it feels crowded.
 UAG 3-in-1 Travel and Desktop Charger
 Photograph: Simon Hill 
 UAG 3-in-1 Travel and Desktop Charger for $165 : This charger was close to earning a top spot until I clocked the price. It’s a very smart 3-in-1 charging kit that folds flat and comes in a snazzy zip-up bag with a 4-foot braided USB-C cable and 25-watt power adapter, including plugs for the US, UK, and Europe. You can prop your iPhone at different angles on the MagSafe stand, and it works well with StandBy mode and Nightstand mode for your Apple Watch, but it’s not Qi2-certified, so you won’t get the stated 15-watt charging for an iPhone. Ultimately, it’s just too expensive.
 Aukey MagFusion Z Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charging Station for $80 : This clever 3-in-1 charging station folds flat and feels durable, but it’s kind of heavy for travel. I found my Apple Watch tended to lean on one side on the charger and didn’t work with Nightstand mode unless I folded it above the main charger, which is also the position required for the iPhone to sit in landscape orientation for StandBy mode.
 Mophie 3-in-1 Travel Charger With MagSafe for $150 : This little travel kit comes with a carrying case, charging brick, and USB-C cable. The square stack unfolds to reveal three wireless chargers in one elongated pad. The iPhone sticks magnetically to the center (15 watts), and the Apple Watch dock supports Nightstand mode. There's also a grooved spot for the AirPods. It feels great, is compact, and is pretty lightweight all around.
 Twelve South Butterfly 2-in-1 MagSafe Charger for $80 : This is an uber compact 2-in-1 charger that looks like a hockey puck. Open the Butterfly, and you'll find two pads that are attached via a rubbery silicone material. You can fast charge an Apple Watch on one—even popping the charger up to take advantage of Nightstand mode—and the other circle lets you recharge your MagSafe iPhone at 15 watts. It's a super compact solution, and Twelve South includes a 30-watt power source and cable with international plug adapters.
 Native Union Voyage 2-in-1 MagSafe Charger for $100 : For a slightly lower price, reviews editor Adrienne So likes Native Union's Qi2 butterfly solution, which doesn't include plug adapters but does come in a tidy travel pouch and has a cable.
 Avoid These Chargers
 Mous Travel Charger : While the compact folding nature of this charger and the low price impressed me, it gets kinda warm when you charge all three of your Apple devices, and the AirPods spot is finicky.
 MagSafe and Qi2, Explained
 AccordionItemContainerButton 
 Most of my picks are MagSafe or Qi2-certified wireless chargers. That means they take advantage of the magnets embedded in the back of the iPhone 12 , iPhone 13 , iPhone 14 , iPhone 15 , iPhone 16 , and iPhone 17 ranges. The magnets ensure perfect alignment, enabling faster and more efficient wireless charging.
 Qi2 is a wireless charging standard that Apple worked with the Wireless Power Consortium to develop. Compared to the original Qi standard, it brings MagSafe-style magnetic charging, enabling faster charging rates and improved efficiency. Apple updated the iPhone 12 and newer to support Qi2, but it’s not just for Apple phones; other phones can get Qi2 certification. While Qi2 Android phones are still thin on the ground, you’ll find Qi2 in Google's Pixel 10 series , and there are Qi2-ready phones that add magnets via a compatible case .
 Qi2 charging mostly goes up to 15 watts, but the Qi2.2 update, branded as Qi2 25W, goes up to 25 watts. Support for Qi2 25W is currently very limited, and includes the iPhone 17 range and the Pixel 10 Pro XL.
 If you use a case, ensure it is a MagSafe or Qi2 compatible case. A normal case will weaken the pull of the magnets in the device and will not stick to chargers as well. If your case is too thick, your phone may not charge at all.
 MagSafe is also available in the AirPods charging case (depending on your model ). Apple's AirPods and AirPods Pro with the wireless charging case will work with nearly all of the standard Qi wireless charging pads on these chargers (as will many third-party wireless earbuds ), but if you have AirPods with MagSafe, then you can hook them up to the magnetic mounts as well.
 What Are StandBy and Nightstand Modes?
 AccordionItemContainerButton 
 I mention StandBy and Nightstand modes throughout this guide, but what are they?
 StandBy mode was introduced in iOS 17 . When you place your iPhone on a charger in landscape orientation, it turns the screen into a smart display to show the time (with different clock designs to choose from), photos from your library, or widgets. If you have an iPhone that supports an always-on screen, you can choose to have the display automatically turn off after a certain amount of time when the iPhone isn't in use or if the room is dark. Head to Settings > Standby to customize it.
 Nightstand mode shows the time on your Apple Watch when the watch is sitting upright and charging, so it can serve as a beside clock. You can customize this on your Apple Watch by heading to Settings > General > Nightstand mode .

 We’ve rounded up the best MagSafe, Qi2, Qi2.2 25W, and MagSafe-compatible magnetic chargers, from the plain pad to multi-functional stands (up to six devices charged), and even the most colorful—from snap-on chargers and modular stands to foldable power banks and full charging desk mats.
 Apple’s MagSafe technology, supported by all models of iPhone since the iPhone 12 (except the iPhone SE and 16e), presents a more efficient way of wirelessly charging compatible iPhones. MagSafe is the ring of magnets around the iPhone’s internal charging coil that senses compatible accessories and magnetically snaps securely into the most efficient charging position with the right accessories. With MagSafe, you’re less likely to wake up to find your phone wasn’t correctly placed on the wireless charger so didn’t charge at all!

 Testing the best for you
 We have tested a lot of magnetic chargers—MagSafe, Qi2 and Compatible—and here inform you which one will work best for you. There are simple magnetic wireless chargers, multi-device chargers for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, travel chargers, car chargers and more.

 Offering up to 25W power output in the right configuration, MagSafe charging is much faster than basic 7.5W magnetic wireless charging. The similar magentic Qi2 standard , supported by the iPhone 13-17 families (and unofficially the iPhone 12 but strangely not the latest 16e) offers similar 15W speed charging. Qi 2.2 , also known as Qi2 25W, meets MagSafe at 25W for iPhone 16/17 series.
 MagSafe or Qi2 certification
 Apple certifies MagSafe accessories to ensures that the output charging is 15W for most iPhones, and up to 25W for iPhone 16 and 17 (with Apple’s latest MagSafe charger or chargers certified for Qi2 25W). Non-certified magnetic but “MagSafe-compatible” chargers are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets to hold your phone in place. Certified MagSafe chargers also have a single-wire NFC antenna that allows the iPhone to identify the device and a built-in magnetometer to prevent compass interference while you are using your iPhone while it’s charging.
 In our tests, 15W MagSafe and Qi2 chargers are evenly matched for charging speeds. 7.5W MagSafe compatible chargers, as you might expect, take around twice as long—certainly in the early stages of charging. But don’t rule out 7.5W chargers as they are often high quality, nearly always noticeably cheaper and just take a while longer to fully charge an iPhone. The king of the hill is Apple’s new MagSafe charger and chargers based on the new Qi2 25W technology that are definitely faster at 25W, but only with iPhone 16 or later.
 Foundry
 Simple vs multi-device magnetic chargers
 The most basic form of MagSafe or magnetic charger is the simple pad that latches on to the compatible iPhone. Some pads feature a pop-out arm so the iPhone can be propped up while charging. There are also products that can simultaneously charge an iPhone plus other Apple devices, such as an Apple Watch or wireless AirPods charging case. Note that the AirPods case must be of the wireless variety, and the original AirPods case lacked this functionality. The base of a multi-charger could also be used to charge a second iPhone but mostly not magnetically and at 5W rather than 7.5W, 15W, or 25W. Also see our round up of the Best Apple Watch chargers and stands .
 Best simple MagSafe chargers
 A simple MagSafe charging pad is the cheapest route to wireless iPhone charging. If you are going to the bother of connecting this product to a wall charger, why not just use a Lightning (iPhone 14 or earlier) or USB-C (iPhone 15 and up) cable direct to the iPhone? You can fast-charge an iPhone to 50% battery in under 30 minutes using a cable and just over that using a 25W charger, while it takes around 50 minutes to wirelessly charge iPhone from 0 to 50% using even 15W MagSafe.
 That said, there are interesting options to choose from. After these we’ll look at more multi-functional MagSafe chargers.

 The most recent NEXA Lift model features an iPhone charger that raises into an adjustable stand.

Alternatively you can charge the MacBook itself while it sits protected in the sleeve—for this you’ll need a more powerful  MacBook charger .
 Read our full 
 Journey NEXA 4-in-1 Laptop Sleeve with Wireless Charging review 
 Why wireless?
 Wireless charging is convenient and fine for situations when you don’t need a super-fast recharge, although the latest 25W wireless chargers are getting close to the power and therefore speed you’ll get from charging via a cable
 If you’re leaving your home in 20 minutes and need as much juice as possible, plug in a cable (USB-C for iPhone 15 or later, or Lightning for earlier iPhones) into a USB-C charger (of at least 30W) to power up an iPhone faster than wireless. With 25W wireless chargers you can simply place your iPhone on and know you should be able to charge it to 50% in around 30 minutes.
 Wireless charging is less wearing than constantly inserting a cable into your phone, and more reliable as that vulnerable cable port can fill with fluff and dust after all the time spent in your trouser pocket or bag and it’s one of the most common reasons that an iPhone refuses to charge even when connected with a cable. It’s easy to clean with a toothpick (but please do it softly!) but will affect most of us at some time. Read our tips about how to clear dirt and fluff from your iPhone’s charging port .
 Wireless charging isn’t affected by the build-up of dust and fluff in the phone port and is also less vulnerable to oxidation and corrosion.
 With wireless, you don’t have to remember to run around trying to find who’s taken your charging cable, and it’s certainly a lot neater.
 Of course, wireless charging is not really wireless, unless you are using a portable magnetic power bank . The magnetic charger is still connected by a cable to your wall charger; it’s just the connection to the phone that is properly wireless.
 What else you need
 Some magnetic chargers come with their own wall charger, but most require you to add your own. Apple recommends at least a 20W USB-C power adapter (wall-socket charger) and we agree unless your charger supports 25W wireless charging, in which case go with at least a 30 USB-C charger or higher if it’s a 2-in-1 or 3-in-1 multi-device charger.

An eight-minute charge will support eight hours of sleep tracking. Without fast charge, it takes about 1.5 hours to charge an Apple Watch to 80%, and about 2.5 hours to 100%.

In our real-world tests using the iOS 26 beta on our iPhone 16 Pro, we saw actual charging times from 0 to 50 percent of 30-35 minutes, measurably faster than 15W MagSafe.

 FAQ 
 1. 
 How much time does Apple Watch take to fast charge? 
 The Apple Watch battery life is notoriously short between charges so fast charging is a great way to keep your smart timepiece topped up and ready for action. 
 Using a Fast Charger cable, you’ll get fully powered up in the shortest time so look for Watch chargers that support fast-charging.
 Apple Watch Series 7, Series 8, and Series 9 : Charge from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
 Apple Watch Series 10 and later : Charge from 0% to 80% in about 30 minutes.
 Apple Watch Ultra and Ultra 2 : Charge from 0% to 80% in about an hour.
 Apple Watch Ultra 3 : Charge from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
 Apple Watch SE 3 : Charges from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
 An eight-minute charge should power your Watch for eight hours of sleep tracking.
 Fast charging requires at least a 20W USB-C charger. 
 See How to fast charge Apple Watch for more information.
 2. 
 Which Apple Watch models can fast charge? 
 The following Apple Watch models support Fast Charge: Apple Watch Series 7, Apple Watch Series 8, Apple Watch Series 9, Series 10, Series 11, Apple Watch Ultra, Ultra 2 and Ultra 3.
 The original Apple Watch SE does not support Fast Charge, but the Apple Watch SE 3 does.
 3. 
 How can I see my Apple Watch battery percentage?
 To see how much power remains on your Apple Watch, hold the bottom of the screen and swipe up to open the Control Center. You can add the battery life percentage to the watch face by adding a battery complication, in this way:
 Hold the display, then tap Edit
 Swipe left to the end to see if the watch face includes a possible battery complication
 Tap the complication to select it, then turn the Digital Crown to choose the battery complication
 To save your changes, press the Digital Crown, then tap the face to switch to it.
 You can also add a battery widget to show the battery percentage of a connected Apple Watch on your iPhone.
 4. 
 How to save battery power on the Apple watch
 When you can’t get to your Apple Watch charger fast enough and the Watch battery is dangerously low, you can eke out the remaining battery charge by saving power.
 The easiest way save battery life is to turn on Low Power Mode . This turns off Always On Display, background heart rate and blood oxygen measurements, plus heart rate notifications. Cellular access is also turned off in Low Power Mode. If you’re just going for a walk, then maybe you don’t need the heart monitor on—although this may impact your Exercise score, it could keep your Watch going till you get back to base and a charging socket.
 To turn on Low Power Mode, tap the side button on your Apple Watch to open Control Center, and select the battery percentage. Then tap Low Power Mode.
 Apple states that “other notifications may be delayed, emergency alerts may not arrive, and certain cellular and Wi-Fi connections are limited” in Low Power Mode. 
 When the Watch battery is charged to 80%, Low Power Mode turns off automatically.
 Other Apple Watch battery saving tips include: 
 Don’t use an Exercise or other tracking. 
 If you are exercising you can still save some battery by turning on Low Power Mode—open the Watch app on your iPhone, and scroll to Workout where you can turn Low Power Mode on by tapping the slider on the right. To further conserve battery life, turn on Fewer GPS and Heart Rate Readings by tapping the slider.
 Turn off Always On Display in the Settings app
 Turn off the Wake Screen so that when you raise the watch to your face the screen doesn’t automatically turn on. Tap the screen or press the Digital Crown to manually wake up the screen instead. Open Settings on your Apple Watch. Select General > Display & Brightness. Turn off Wake on Wrist Raise by tapping the slider.
 Turn off background apps: push the side button (not the digital crown) and release it; then scroll through the running apps using the digital crown; close the apps by swiping from left to right and tapping on the “X”
 Turn off the heart rate monitor and advanced health tracking in the Watch app on your iPhone: Privacy
 Turn off voice assistant Siri—which is always listening for your commands—in Apple Watch Settings
 Turn on Theater mode, which prevents the Apple Watch display from turning on when you raise your wrist, and also turns on Silent Mode
 Turn on Silent Mode
 Use a darker watch face as black pixels use less power than bright ones such as Mickey Mouse or the Activity Face
 In extreme circumstances when you know you’ll need your Apple Watch later but not right now, turn off your Apple Watch by pressing and holding the side button until you see the Power Off slider
 Unpair AirPods from your Apple Watch in Settings.
 Always keep your Watch software up to date. Some Watch software updates are specifically to improve battery life, while others keep your Watch operating as efficiently as possible. In the Watch app on your iPhone, go to My Watch > General > Software Update.
 Optimized Battery Charging is turned on by default when you set up your Apple Watch, but check it’s on by opening Settings on the Apple Watch,a nd then selecting Battery > Battery Health. Turn Optimized Battery Charging on via the slider. See more on Optimized Battery Charging below.
 See: How to improve Apple Watch battery life for more advice. 
 5. 
 How to turn on Low Power Mode on the Apple Watch
 When its battery charge falls to 10% or lower, your Apple Watch alerts you and suggests that you enter Low Power Mode. 
 Hold the bottom of the Watch screen, then swipe up to open Control Center.
 Tap the battery percentage icon, then turn on Low Power Mode.
 Scroll down, and tap Turn On Low Power Mode.
 6. 
 Optimize Apple Watch Charging
 The Apple Watch Optimized Battery Charging feature uses on-device machine learning to discover your charging habits over time along with your daily usage to either charge the Watch to an optimized level or charge it to full in order to improve the lifespan of your Watch battery.
 This will slow down the wear on your Watch battery to improve its lifespan by reducing the time your Apple Watch spends fully charged. When turned on, your watch delays charging past 80% in certain situations, so that the battery level remains between 75-80%. Optimised Battery Charging is only activated when your watch predicts it will be connected to a charger for an extended period of time, and still aims to ensure your Apple Watch is fully charged when removed from the charger.
 If, for example, you mostly leave your Watch on charge overnight, Optimised Battery Charging will slow down the charging to make it more efficient over the period you are usually asleep, while still making sure that the battery is full and ready for your daytime usage by the time you wake up.

 Key takeaways 
 A genuine 3-in-1 Apple charging station charges an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously; these docks do not provide a wireless iPad charging surface.
 Phone charging ranges from 7.5W Qi and 15W MagSafe or Qi2 to a manufacturer-rated 25W Qi2 on selected newer products.
 Maximum charging speed depends on the exact iPhone, charging standard, case, software, alignment, and power adapter.
 Apple Watch charging is a separate compatibility question: look for explicit Apple Watch Fast Charging support rather than assuming a generic Qi pad will work.
 Included power supplies change the value substantially; Belkin, Twelve South, and Nimble document adapters bundled with the reviewed models.
 Foldable stations are easier to pack, while vertical stands are generally better for desks, nightstands, StandBy, and glanceable notifications.
 What is the best 3-in-1 charging station for iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods? 
 The best 3-in-1 charging station for iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods depends on the buyer’s priority: Belkin’s UltraCharge Pro targets the highest advertised iPhone output, Anker’s 3-in-1 Cube is the most travel-friendly, Twelve South’s HiRise 3 Deluxe is the strongest vertical-stand choice, mophie’s stand emphasizes adjustable viewing and silent operation, and Nimble’s Podium combines 15W charging with recycled materials.
 This is a researched shortlist of five models, not a claim that ten independently tested products could be ranked. The available product evidence consists primarily of manufacturer and Apple retail specifications rather than a shared laboratory test, so the recommendations below describe documented features and use-case fit rather than declaring an objectively fastest or most durable charger.

 Lcssio 300W Charging Station for Multiple Devices, 8 Port Fast Charger | Fast Charging, Safety Certified, Compact Design, Organized Charging, Multiple Devices at Once, With 6 Cables 
 8 Port Charging Station for Multiple Devices: Our multi charging station comes with 5 USB-C ports to accommodate modern devices compared to those charging stations which only have USB-A ports. This charging dock shares a total output up to 300W with dual 65w ports to charge laptops. Its extra 30w and 20w ports can power tablets and smartphones.
 Sturdy Slots: The housing body of this charging station is all together with solid construction and cannot be disassembled. We don’t add those cheap removable flimsy dividers.  How to choose the right station 
 Identify the exact iPhone. Do not select a charger solely by its maximum wattage. Confirm whether the phone supports the advertised MagSafe or Qi2 mode.
 Check Apple Watch support separately. Look for a dedicated Apple Watch charging module and explicit Fast Charging language if fast watch charging matters.
 Decide whether the station stays put. A foldable design is convenient in luggage; a vertical stand is usually easier to use repeatedly on a desk or nightstand.
 Calculate complete setup cost. Include a USB-C wall adapter if the exact package does not supply one, and check the adapter’s wattage.
 Check case and alignment compatibility. Thick, misaligned, or non-compatible cases can reduce or interrupt magnetic wireless charging.
 Separate documented specifications from marketing tests. Treat Belkin’s 0–50% in 25 minutes statement as a manufacturer test claim, not a universal result.
 Verify the generation before ordering. In particular, distinguish the original Twelve South HiRise 3 Deluxe from the HiRise 3 Deluxe Qi2, and distinguish Anker’s Cube from its other MagGo and Prime foldable stations.
 Bottom line 
 For the highest advertised compatible iPhone output, choose the Belkin UltraCharge Pro. For a compact travel charger, choose the Anker 3-in-1 Cube with Qi2. For a vertical desk or nightstand, choose the original Twelve South HiRise 3 Deluxe; for an adjustable fanless stand, consider mophie; and for recycled materials plus an included wall charger, consider Nimble Podium.

 Frequently Asked Questions

 Do 3-in-1 chargers come with a wall adapter?

 Qi2 25W can provide a higher advertised phone output than 15W MagSafe or 15W Qi2, but only compatible phones and setups can use the maximum. The phone model, case, alignment, software, temperature, and adapter all affect actual charging.
 Can I charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time?
 Yes, the reviewed stations are designed to charge an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously using separate charging positions. Simultaneous charging does not guarantee that every device receives its maximum rated speed at the same time.
 The Bottom Line 
 Best overall by use case: Belkin for maximum documented phone speed, Anker for travel, Twelve South for a vertical stand, mophie for adjustable fanless charging, and Nimble for recycled materials with a bundled 35W adapter. All five are for iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods—not wireless iPad charging.

 Belkin’s stand holds the iPhone magnetically on an upright arm, with an Apple Watch charger and an AirPods pad below. It charges the phone at up to 25W, the watch quickly enough that Belkin quotes 0 to 80% for an Apple Watch Series 10 in about 45 minutes, and AirPods at up to 5W. It has a weighted chrome base and a small fan with an on/off switch that runs only when a device is attached. That fan is what lets it keep charging fast without overheating.
 The one to buy for a nightstand or desk Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 charging station, Black A weighted nightstand stand that charges iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods together, with a fan for 25W speeds. Qi2.2 up to 25W Active cooling fan Apple Watch fast charging StandBy Check price on Amazon 
 Two caveats. First, a fan can make a light hum, which Belkin itself acknowledges. If you are a light sleeper, use the switch, accept slower charging overnight, or choose the passively cooled foldable model. Second, it is a large object for a small nightstand. Measure first if space is tight.
 The stand works with StandBy, which turns a charging iPhone on its side into a clock, photo frame or widget display. That is one of the best reasons to choose an upright stand over a flat pad.
 Best for travel: Belkin Qi2.2 25W Foldable 3-in-1
 The foldable model packs flat for a bag and still charges the iPhone at up to 25W, with Belkin quoting 0 to 50% in about 29 minutes. The stand angle adjusts up to 65 degrees for portrait or landscape, and the iPhone can still charge while the stand is folded. It uses passive cooling, so there is no fan to hear.
 For travel, or one charger for home and bag Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 foldable charger Charges an iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods from one stand, and folds for travel. Qi2.2 25W 3 devices Foldable Check price on Amazon 
 The trade-off is stability. A folding stand is lighter and easier to knock over than a weighted base, and passive cooling means it can slow down sooner in a warm room. For a hotel room or a second desk, it is the more useful design.

 If you only charge two devices: Apple’s chargers
 A 3-in-1 only earns its space if you use all three spots. Many people charge AirPods rarely, from a USB-C cable or in a case that lasts days. For them, Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger are the cleaner setup.
 Apple’s 1m MagSafe Charger for the iPhone Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m) Apple’s own magnetic iPhone charger, for people who only need to charge a phone. MagSafe Up to 25W on supported iPhones 1 m cable Check price on Amazon 
 Apple’s fast charger for Apple Watch Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger to USB-C Cable (1 m) Apple’s woven fast charger for Apple Watch, used with a USB-C power adapter. Fast charging USB-C 1 m woven cable Check price on Amazon 
 Apple says its watch charger is fast-charging capable with an Apple 20W USB-C adapter, and quotes, for example, 18 hours of use for Apple Watch Ultra 4 from 15 minutes of charging. You will need two power adapters or a multi-port charger. Our guide to the best USB-C chargers covers compact multi-port bricks that can power both.

 Does your case work with a magnetic stand?
 Thin cases with their own MagSafe magnets work fine. Thick rugged cases, wallets, grips and rings attached to the back of the phone can weaken the magnetic hold or stop charging entirely. If you use a PopSocket-style grip, check whether it is designed to stay on while charging; many need removing.
 Apple Watch bands matter too. Some 3-in-1 stands put the watch charger close to the base, and a closed loop or metal link band may not let the watch lie flat. Stands like Belkin’s with a raised watch puck generally handle open bands better.
 What to skip
 Skip unbranded 3-in-1 stands that do not state Qi2 or Qi2.2 certification. They often use weaker magnets, charge at 7.5W or 15W, and run hot. Skip chargers that use a flat AirPods pad if your AirPods case does not support wireless charging. And skip a 3-in-1 entirely if you will only ever charge your phone on it: a single MagSafe charger is cheaper and takes up less room.

 How to choose the right station

 Choose a verified 25W Qi2 or MagSafe station if speed matters, especially for daytime top-ups. Choose 15W Qi2 if the phone charges overnight, sits on a desk for long periods or you want to spend less.

 Do not infer 25W from the word “Qi2.” Qi2 products can be 15W or 25W. Likewise, “MagSafe compatible” can describe magnetic alignment without promising Apple’s maximum charging performance. The product card should identify the actual rated output.
 Qi2 versus MagSafe
 MagSafe is Apple’s magnetic charging and accessory system. Qi2 is an industry wireless-charging standard with magnetic alignment in compatible implementations. They overlap in practical use but are not interchangeable labels for speed or certification.
 For a current iPhone 17-series purchase, look for a specific 25W Qi2 or MagSafe rating, not merely a magnetic ring or “MagSafe-style” description.
 Do you need a 2-in-1 or 3-in-1?
 1-in-1: best for one phone, travel and minimum cost.
 2-in-1: best for an iPhone plus Apple Watch or AirPods.
 3-in-1: best for an iPhone, Watch and AirPods on one desk or bedside table.
 Modular or 4-in-1: best for families and mixed-device homes, but usually less compact and more dependent on separate charging pucks.
 Check the wall adapter separately
 A charger’s output and its power supply are different specifications. A station can advertise 25W while requiring a separately purchased adapter capable of delivering enough input. Anker explicitly requires 45W or higher for full 25W output on its Prime station.
 Before buying, record four separate facts: whether the adapter is included, the recommended adapter wattage, whether a USB-C cable is included and whether full output requires a particular cable or charging protocol.

 Is active cooling worth it?
 Active cooling can help manage heat during higher-power charging, but it adds cost, fan noise, moving parts, dust exposure and bulk. It makes the most sense for 25W charging, warm environments, frequent top-ups or charging while using navigation and other demanding functions. For overnight charging, a quiet passive station is often the better fit.
 Will it hold an iPhone 17 Pro Max?
 No special charging standard is required for the Pro Max, but its larger, heavier body makes poor hardware more obvious. A good station should remain stable when the phone is attached and removed one-handed, hold the phone in portrait and landscape, avoid hinge droop and leave clearance for the camera bump.
 Test or verify the station with a case fitted. Weak magnets, narrow hinges and lightweight bases are more likely to cause sagging or tipping with the Pro Max.
 Will it work through a case?
 Expect the best results with a thin MagSafe or Qi2 case. Thick rugged cases, metal plates, wallet attachments, battery cases and poorly aligned magnetic rings can reduce charging speed or prevent charging. Do not promise universal case compatibility unless the manufacturer explicitly specifies it and the product has been checked.
 Does it include an Apple Watch charger?
 “Apple Watch compatible” can mean three different things:

 This distinction can change the real cost of a 3-in-1 station. Belkin’s modular Qi2 25W dock, for example, uses a holder for an official smartwatch charger but does not include the Apple Watch charger.
 Independent reader support Your contribution helps us test, update, and keep practical guides available for everyone. Support on Ko-Fi Common problems and fixes
 The station charges slowly even though it says 25W
 Check that the wall adapter meets the station’s input requirement.
 Confirm that the exact model is Qi2 25W rather than Qi2 15W.
 Remove thick cases, wallets, rings and metal plates.
 Center the phone carefully on the magnetic mount.
 Allow the phone to cool; temperature, battery level and heavy use can reduce output.
 Check the cable and regional product specifications.
 The phone disconnects overnight
 Look for camera-bump interference, a weak or misaligned case magnet, cable movement, an uneven surface or a stand angle that lets the phone slide. Try the station without the case to isolate alignment from charger problems.
 The Apple Watch does not charge
 Confirm that a Watch puck is actually included, that it is seated correctly and that the holder supports your Watch model and case. A storage recess is not necessarily a charging module.
 AirPods do not charge
 The AirPods case must support wireless charging and sit over the correct coil. Protective cases, poor centering and a generic pad with no dedicated recess can all cause intermittent charging.
 What not to overvalue
 Do not treat a manufacturer’s charging-time claim as an independent test. Belkin and Anker publish charging claims under stated conditions; actual results vary with the adapter, cable, temperature, software, battery level, case and use during charging.
 Also avoid claims that a station is “best for battery health,” “silent” or compatible with every case unless the evidence supports that exact wording. A manufacturer’s claim that a fan operates at 19 dB should be attributed rather than converted into an unconditional “silent” verdict.

 The fastest 3-in-1 docks now advertise 25W phone output, but the useful speed depends on the exact iPhone. The key dividing line is whether a dock supports the phone’s ceiling and whether its maker lists that model as compatible.
 Apple lists up to 25W for iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max; iPhone Air tops out at 20W

 # What Does iPhone 17 Get From a 3-in-1 Charger?
 iPhone 17 negotiates wireless speed off the pad’s certification, the adapter’s wattage, and (with Qi2.2) thermal headroom in the dock itself.
 The model split matters more than the family name. According to Apple’s MagSafe support article , iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max can reach 25W with Apple’s current MagSafe Charger. The same page lists 20W for iPhone Air, 22.5W for iPhone 16 and 16 Pro, 25W for iPhone 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max, and 15W for iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 or earlier.
 A 3-in-1 dock also has to feed Apple Watch and AirPods at the same time.
 That changes the adapter decision. A dock has to divide its input among the phone pad, Watch puck, and AirPods pad, and manufacturers size that budget differently. Use the dock maker’s bundled or recommended adapter instead of applying one universal wattage threshold.
 A few buying details that matter.
 Watch puck must be Apple-fast-charge certified to cut overnight top-ups in half. Generic Qi pads ignore the fast-charge negotiation and trickle the Watch at standard speed. Our Apple Watch battery drain breakdown explains why overnight charging behavior matters.
 AirPods get the same flat 5W Qi pad on every dock in this roundup, with no MagSafe magnet on the AirPods position.
 Form factor matters for desk real estate. A foldable or cube uses less surface area than a flat 3-pad slab. Pair it with our best GaN charger coverage if the dock doesn’t include an adapter.
 # Best Overall 3-in-1: Anker Prime (Qi2.2 25W)
 The Anker Prime 3-in-1 is the foldable 25W-rated option in this roundup. It best fits iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max owners who want the dock maker’s highest advertised phone output in a unit that fits a sleeve pocket; iPhone Air remains limited to 20W by the phone.

 Travel form factor is the killer feature here.
 Folded, the stand is roughly the size of a closed sunglass case. Open, it tilts the phone in landscape for StandBy mode while keeping the Watch and AirPods pads accessible.
 Buyer review count is the second reason to consider this pick. 4,000+ verified reviews found that the fast-charge claim holds up on real Apple Watch Ultra units, not just the marketing spec sheet.
 # Qi2 vs Qi2.2: Which Spec Matters for 3-in-1?
 Two generations matter here.
 Qi2 established a 15W magnetic charging tier, while newer 25W-rated accessories raise the advertised ceiling for compatible phones. Apple’s own model matrix is not a simple Pro-versus-standard split, so check both the phone ceiling and the third-party dock’s compatibility list.
 For iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 or earlier, a 15W Qi2 dock already reaches Apple’s listed ceiling. Newer iPhone 16 and 17 models split across 20W, 22.5W, and 25W tiers, so a blanket family rule gives the wrong buying advice.
 Phone model Apple-listed MagSafe maximum Buying implication 
 iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max 25W Verify the third-party dock supports 25W 
 iPhone Air 20W A 25W-rated dock doesn’t raise the 20W cap 
 iPhone 17e 15W A 15W Qi2 dock is sufficient 
 iPhone 16 Plus / 16 Pro Max 25W Verify the third-party dock supports 25W 
 iPhone 16 / 16 Pro 22.5W Check the dock’s model-specific rating 
 iPhone 15 and earlier Up to 15W A 15W Qi2 dock is sufficient for most 
 Wireless charging ceiling by iPhone model for 2026. 
 The Anker Prime and Belkin BoostCharge Pro are the two 25W-rated picks in this roundup. The Anker MagGo Cube and Foldable Stand remain 15W Qi2 options, which is enough for iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 or earlier but leaves speed unused on several iPhone 16 and 17 models.
 For PD adapter context, our best GaN charger for iPhone 16 roundup covers cheap fast bricks that pair well with a Qi2 dock if you’d rather buy the adapter separately.
 # How 3-in-1 Docks Affect Apple Watch Battery Health
 Short answer: not if you use one with Apple-fast-charge certification.
 Apple explains in its Optimized Battery Charging support page that Apple Watch may delay charging past 80% when it predicts the watch will remain connected to a charger for an extended period, then finish before it expects you to remove it.
 The risk vector is heat.
 If you stack a 3-in-1 on top of a desktop computer (or any warm surface), the bottom pad runs hotter than spec and thermal throttling kicks the Watch down to standard charge speed. Our Apple Watch battery drain guide covers what to do if you see steady capacity loss after a few months of dock use.
 For thermal context on the iPhone side, see our iPhone overheating while charging guide.
 # Bottom Line
 iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max owners should consider the Anker Prime 3-in-1 when they want a foldable dock rated for 25W on compatible models. iPhone Air owners can use the same dock, but Apple’s listed ceiling for that phone is 20W.
 For iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 17e, the Anker MagGo Cube is the 15W value pick.
 Pick the Belkin BoostCharge Pro if Apple Store warranty access matters more than form factor: same Qi2.2 25W output as the Prime but stocked in physical Apple Stores. Pick the Foldable Stand if Apple Watch Ultra fast-charge is the deciding spec.
 For the single-pad MagSafe puck pick, see our best MagSafe charger for iPhone 17 roundup.
 # Frequently Asked Questions
 Can a 3-in-1 dock fast-charge all three devices at once? + 
 Yes, if the dock and its power adapter are designed to run all three outputs together.
 Use the bundled adapter or the wattage the dock maker recommends. Total input needs differ by phone-output tier, Watch hardware, and the dock’s internal power allocation.
 Do I need Qi2.2 if I have an iPhone 16? + 
 It depends on the iPhone 16 model. Apple lists up to 22.5W for iPhone 16 and 16 Pro, and up to 25W for iPhone 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max with its current MagSafe Charger.
 A third-party 25W-rated dock still needs explicit compatibility with your exact model. A 15W Qi2 dock works, but it won’t reach those higher Apple-listed ceilings.
 Will a 3-in-1 dock work with my AirPods Max? + 
 The AirPods pad on every dock in this roundup is a flat 5W Qi pad sized for the AirPods or AirPods Pro case. AirPods Max charge over Lightning or USB-C cable, not wirelessly, so they won’t fit on the third pad.
 Are 3-in-1 docks safe to leave plugged in 24/7? + 
 Yes, with Optimized Battery Charging enabled on iPhone and watchOS, a 3-in-1 dock is safe for 24/7 use. The dock pulls less than 1W when no devices are charging, and Optimized Charging may delay charging past 80% in certain situations to reduce time spent fully charged. If you’re worried about long-term battery health, see our iPhone fast charging and battery health guide for the underlying chemistry.
 What’s the difference between Qi2 and MagSafe on a 3-in-1? + 
 Both use magnetic alignment, but their certifications and supported power tiers are not interchangeable promises. A charger’s advertised maximum does not guarantee the same speed on every iPhone.
 Check the iPhone model’s Apple-listed ceiling and the third-party maker’s compatibility list. Those two facts, plus the recommended adapter, determine the practical speed.
 Why does my 3-in-1 charge AirPods slower than my single-pad MagSafe? + 
 The third pad on every 3-in-1 in this roundup is a flat 5W Qi pad without MagSafe magnets, while Apple’s first-party MagSafe puck negotiates a slightly higher speed on the AirPods Pro case. The difference is roughly 10-15 minutes on a full case top-up.
 If your AirPods aren’t charging at all on the third pad, see our AirPods case not charging troubleshooting guide.
 Can I use a 3-in-1 dock for Pixel 10 or other Android phones? + 
 Only if the dock is Qi2 certified and your Android phone supports Qi2 (Pixel 10 does, most older Android phones don’t). The Apple Watch and AirPods pads won’t work with anything non-Apple.
 The Belkin BoostCharge Pro is the most explicit about Pixel 10 support in this roundup.

 What’s different about the designs?
 All the portable models are designed for travel, folding up neatly to fit into matching compact travel cases. You can arrive at your destination without the usual tangled mess of cables.
 The smallest folded Mophie travel charger is the Gen 3, available in the great multi-colored version we’ve tested here and also black if all the fun has drained out of your life. It also features the bi-fold design that takes up less desk space when unfolded. The tri-fold unfolds to a length of nearly a foot across, while the bi-fold measures half that when laid out. That’s because the AirPods charging pad on the bi-fold is hidden behind the more able iPhone adjustable charging stand.
 Simon Jary
 The Roam and Orange/Teal 3-in-1 Travel Charger differ from the Black and Pink versions by hosting the AirPods charging pad behind the orange adjustable iPhone wireless charging stand. This bi-fold design gives it a smaller footprint when opened up, compared to the older models’ longer strip.
 The Pink and Black models charge the iPhone only in a flat position, but all three allow the Watch to sit up in Nightstand Mode. The Roam and Orange/Teal models features the stand but can also charge the iPhone flat if you prefer.
 The stand for the Roam and Orange chargers is fine for setting the iPhone in a landscape/horizontal StandBy Mode, but less successful with the iPhone is in portrait/vertical when the magnetic placement makes the Watch part lift slightly.
 Simon Jary
 How fast can they charge your devices?
 The main benefit of the latest Roam travel charger is its more powerful Qi2.2 wireless charging output that means iPhones 16 or later can charge at up to 25W. It beats most other 25W 3-in-1 travel chargers through its StealthCharge technology that protects the phone from the heat generated by such powerful wireless charging by moving the potentially hot components away from the phone charging pad.
 Older iPhones  don’t support 25W wireless charging, so remain at Qi2/MagSafe’s 15W maximum. Even then, StealthCharge might make 15W charging a little more efficient, too.
 Simon Jary
 The other Mophie travel chargers are all rated at 15W for all iPhones (12 and later).
 While the black Gen 1 charger can reach 5W for fast-charging the Apple Watch, the others support 7.5W charging, which should mean you can put your Watch back on your wrist sooner. The gen 1 charger is also marginally slower powering up compatible AirPods.
 How much does each travel charger cost?
 Look around as while all the chargers have official retail prices at $149.95, pricing can be cheaper as the products get older—but not always. It would be great to have a mid-ranged product between the premium and super-affordable. It’s likely that the company is selling off the last of the 2021-vintage Gen 1 so stocks will run dry at some stage.
 You’ll find the gen 4 Mophie Roam at Apple for $149.95 or £119.95 , or buy it direct from Mophie or Zagg UK .
 If you are as taken by the Mophie Orange/Teal Special Edition Gen 3 travel charger as I am, it’s still officially priced at $149.95 or £149.95 , or check Amazon .
 Note that Roam and Orange comes with a 40W wall charger and international plug adapters, while the pink and black travel chargers ship with just a 30W charger, All come with a matching travel case.
 Fancy the pretty pink Cherry Blossom Mophie Gen 2 travel charger ? Zagg is still selling it as $149.95 or you can find it at Amazon .
 If you are after the lowest cost and don’t care for joyful colorways, you can find the Mophie Gen 1 for $39 at Zagg, or $49.95 at Amazon. The cheapest we could find it in the U.K. was £61 at Amazon.
 We’ve tested more of the best 3-in-1 iPhone/Watch/AirPods chargers for further comparisons.
 Which Mophie 3-in-1 Travel Charger should you buy?
 At 25W the Gen 4 Roam is the fastest of all the Mophie travel chargers, although only for iPhones 16 and later. If you aren’t planning on upgrading your iPhone for a while and are happy with 15W charging, consider one of the other models in their fun colors. You may have guessed that the 15W Orange/Teal Gen 3 is a particular favorite—it shares a similar design to the Roam but radically different color scheme, and it’s certainly hard to miss. If you’re more a lover of pink, the Gen 2 Cherry Blossom charger will definitely be for you, but for the cheapest price the original Gen 1 Mophie Travel Charger is hard to beat for budgets.

Best 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station for iPhone in 2026: MagSafe 15W Picks Under $40 (iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods)
Charging & Power
Best 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station for iPhone in 2026: MagSafe 15W Picks Under $40 (iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods)
GizToo Team
June 6, 2026
7 min read

TL;DR: The best 3-in-1 wireless charging station for iPhone in 2026 is a Qi2-certified 15W MagSafe-compatible stand with a genuine Apple Watch fast-charging puck, a Qi pad for AirPods, and a single USB-C PD input that needs at least a 30W charger in the box. Under $40 the strongest picks come from Anker MagGo, Belkin BoostCharge Pro, ESR HaloLock, INIU and Yootech. Vertical foldable stands win for nightstands and travel; flat tray pads win for desks. Skip: anything that says "MagSafe compatible" but charges at 7.5W, stations without a real Apple Watch puck (slow Qi-only charging), and any station that doesn't include a 30W+ USB-C PD charger in the box.

The 3-in-1 wireless charging station is one of the most cluttered categories in the iPhone accessory market. Half the listings on Amazon use "MagSafe" as marketing while delivering 7.5W Qi — half the speed of a real Qi2 puck. The Apple Watch slot is often a generic Qi pad that charges your Series 9 or Ultra 2 at the slow 2.5W speed instead of the fast-charging 5W it deserves. And almost none of them include a charger powerful enough in the box to actually run all three pads at full speed simultaneously.

The good news: in 2026, the Qi2 standard (which is essentially MagSafe with a different name, licensed to other brands) finally puts genuine 15W magnetic charging on third-party stations for under $40. Pair that with a real Apple Watch puck and a Qi pad for AirPods, and you have one cable, three devices, and a clear nightstand.

What "3-in-1" actually means in 2026

A proper 3-in-1 charging station has three distinct charging surfaces, each optimized for one device:

iPhone pad/puck — must be Qi2 certified for 15W magnetic charging. Anything labeled only "Qi" or "MagSafe compatible" without the Qi2 logo will fall back to 7.5W on iPhone 12 and newer.
Apple Watch puck — must be a real magnetic puck, ideally Apple-certified (MFW). Generic Qi pads only do 2.5W; a proper puck does 5W fast charging on Series 7 and later, refilling the Watch in about 75 minutes instead of 2.5 hours.
AirPods pad — a flat Qi 5W spot. AirPods don't need more than 5W and don't support MagSafe, so this is the simplest of the three.

If any one of those three is faked, you don't have a 3-in-1 — you have a 1.5-in-1 with two slow trickle chargers. For background on the iPhone side, see our wireless chargers under $40 guide and the MagSafe accessories roundup.

5 categories for different setups
1. Best overall — Qi2 15W vertical stand with real Watch puck

The nightstand sweet spot. A vertical Qi2 puck holds iPhone in landscape so StandBy mode works as a bedside clock and weather display, the Apple Watch puck sits at the right height for Nightstand mode, and the AirPods pad is at the base. One USB-C cable to a 30W brick. Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (Qi2), Belkin BoostCharge Pro 3-in-1 (Qi2) and ESR HaloLock 3-in-1 all hit this spec for $35-40.

2. Best budget — 15W magnetic + 5W Watch pad under $25

The compromise pick: Qi2 15W magnetic for iPhone (real fast charging) but a Qi 5W pad for the Watch instead of a proper puck. Charges Series 6 and earlier at full speed, but slow on Series 7-10 and Ultra. Fine if you charge overnight. INIU, Yootech and most rebrand-friendly Amazon brands sit here under $25.

3. Best for nightstand with StandBy mode — landscape orientation + dim mode

iOS 17+ StandBy mode turns your iPhone into a bedside clock, photo frame or smart display when charging on its side. A station with a wide magnetic puck that holds the phone in landscape, plus a built-in red night mode that dims any LEDs on the station, makes the difference between a useful nightstand and a glowing distraction. Belkin BoostCharge Pro and Twelve South HiRise 3 lead here.

4. Best for travel — foldable 3-in-1 that fits in a backpack pocket

Folds flat to passport size and unfolds into a stand. Lower wattage (usually 7.5W for iPhone) but unbeatable for a 3-day trip when you can't fit three separate chargers in a packing cube. Anker 3-in-1 Cube and ESR Travel 3-in-1 are the established picks. Pair with a small GaN brick instead of the included cable for fastest results.

5. Best for Android + multi-device households — Qi2 universal 15W

Qi2 is not Apple-only. Samsung Galaxy S24/S25, Pixel 9, and other Android flagships will charge at 15W on a Qi2 station with the right magnetic case (or aligned manually on the puck). If your household mixes iPhone and Android, a Qi2 station beats a proprietary MagSafe-only design. Anker MagGo Qi2 stations and the upcoming Belkin Qi2.2 lineup both work universally.

What to look for under $40
Qi2 certification, not "MagSafe compatible"

"MagSafe compatible" is marketing language that only guarantees the magnets line up. Qi2 is the actual standard with the 15W certified output. Look for the Qi2 logo on the box or product page, not just a "works with MagSafe" sticker.

Real Apple Watch puck, not a generic Qi pad

If the Watch slot looks like a flat circle with a Qi coil, it's not fast charging. A real puck is recessed, magnetic, and grips the back of the Watch firmly. MFW (Made for Apple Watch) certification guarantees 5W fast charging on Series 7 and later.

Included charger wattage

To run 15W iPhone + 5W Watch + 5W AirPods at full speed simultaneously, the station needs at least 25-30W at the wall. Many bargain stations ship with a 20W USB-A brick that throttles the iPhone pad to 7.5W when the Watch and AirPods are also charging. Confirm the included charger is USB-C PD 30W or higher, or budget for a separate one.

Cooling: passive vs active fan

15W magnetic charging generates real heat. Most stations rely on passive aluminum heat-spreading, which is fine on a desk but borderline in a hot bedroom. A few premium stations (Belkin BoostCharge Pro Qi2.2) add a tiny silent fan for sustained 15W. Worth the $10 extra if your room runs warm.

Cable length and angle

Check whether the USB-C input enters from the back (clean cable management against the wall) or the side (cable sticks out awkwardly). Stations with at least a 1.5 m cable give you flexibility on where to plug in.

Mistakes to avoid
Buying for "wattage on paper" — a station that says "30W total" might split as 7.5W + 15W + 7.5W instead of giving the iPhone the full 15W. Check the per-pad spec.
Ignoring the included charger — a "free" 18W USB-A brick will bottleneck the entire station. Either confirm 30W PD is included or buy separately.
Trusting Amazon "MagSafe" claims — only Apple-licensed MagSafe and Qi2-certified stations deliver 15W. Everything else is 7.5W.
Skipping the Watch puck check — if your Watch is Series 7 or newer, a generic pad means 2-3× longer charge time.
Putting it next to a hot air vent or in direct sun — wireless charging derates aggressively above 35 °C ambient. Place the station in a shaded, ventilated spot.
